dervis-irab:1-7.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُفْتَنُونَ): they are tested; from fatana fulānan, yaftinuhu, of the pattern of ḍaraba:
he tested him, burned him and led him astray. One says fatana al-ṣāʾigh al-dhahab: the goldsmith melted the gold in the crucible to test it and to distinguish the good from the bad. One also says fatanahu, yaftinuhu, likewise of the pattern of ḍaraba: it charmed him, won him over and threw him into temptation (fitna).

* I'rab:
(الم، أَحَسِبَ النَّاسُ أَنْ يُتْرَكُوا أَنْ يَقُولُوا آمَنَّا وَهُمْ لا يُفْتَنُونَ): (ألم): its i'rab and the discussion of it and of the openings of the surahs have preceded. In (أحسب) the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation or of rebuke, and (حسب) is a past verb that puts two objects in the accusative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Reckoning (ḥusbān) cannot properly be attached to the meanings of single words, but only to the contents of clauses", and that is why it needs two objects. (الناس) is the fāʿil (agent); (أن) and what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of (حسب); (أن يقولوا) is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) if the preposition is supplied as bāʾ; you may also supply the preposition as lām, so that it gives the reason for the leaving, attached to it, i.e. "because of their saying". The clause (آمنا) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the wāw is circumstantial; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause (لا يفتنون) is the khabar (predicate) of (هم), and the clause is circumstantial. The meaning of the verse is: Did those who uttered the word of testimony reckon that they would be left untested? No, rather they will be tested, so that the one firmly rooted in religion may be distinguished from others. This is one of several parsings, which we consider the easiest of them. We present here al-Zamakhsharī's wording for its preciousness. He said:
"Its implied form is: Did they reckon their being left untempted because of their saying 'we believe'? So 'the leaving' is the first of the two objects of حسب, and 'because of their saying we believe' is the khabar. As for 'untempted', it is the complement of 'leaving', which is in the sense of 'making [something] become', as in his saying «فتركنه جزر السباع ينشنه» (so they left him a prey for the beasts, which tear at him). Do you not see that before bringing in the reckoning you are able to say: 'their being left untempted is because of their saying we believe', on the supposition of 'occurring' and 'established' before the lām? If you say: 'that they say' is the reason for their being left untempted, so how can it properly occur as the khabar of a mubtadaʾ? I say: just as you say 'his going out is for fear of evil' and 'his beating is for discipline', whereas the discipline and the fear were two reasons in your saying 'I went out for fear of evil' and 'I beat him for discipline'. You also say 'I reckoned his going out to be for fear of evil' and 'I supposed his beating to be for discipline', making them two objects just as you made them a mubtadaʾ and khabar." More of the discussions of this verse will come in the section on benefits.
(وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ الْكاذِبِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (فتنا) is a verb and its agent; (الذين) is its object; (من قبلهم) are attached to an omitted [verb] that is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين). The fāʾ is a conjunction; the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (ليعلمن) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; (الله) is the agent; (الذين) is its object and the clause (صدقوا) the ṣila; and (ليعلمن الكاذبين) is conjoined to what precedes. The secret of the difference between (صدقوا) and (الكاذبين) will come in the section on rhetoric. The meaning is that temptation and testing are two things indispensable for trying creatures, and created beings have been exposed to them in the various circumstances of time and place. (أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئاتِ أَنْ يَسْبِقُونا ساءَ ما يَحْكُمُونَ): (أم) is disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa), meaning "rather"; it is for transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī), and a hamza must be implied within it, for affirmation and rebuke. (حسب) is a past verb; (الذين) is the agent; the clause (يعملون السيئات) is the ṣila; (أن) and what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of (حسب). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: Where are the two objects of حسب?
I say: The inclusion in the ṣila of أن of a predicate and a subject stands in place of the two objects, as in His saying, Exalted is He, «أم حسبتم أن تدخلوا الجنة». It is also permissible for حسب to be made to contain the meaning of qaddara (to estimate). أم is disjunctive, and the meaning of digression in it is that this reckoning is more false than the first reckoning, because that one estimates that he will not be tested for his faith, while this one supposes that he will not be recompensed for his evil deeds." (ساء) is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame, and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it"; (ما) is an indefinite noun, accusative as a tamyīz (specification); the clause (يحكمون) is its adjective; and the one specified for blame is omitted, i.e. "their judgment". (ما) may also be parsed as a relative noun, the agent, with the clause (يحكمون) its ṣila. It may also be maṣdariyya, i.e. "their judging", and on this view the tamyīz is omitted, i.e. "evil as a judgment is their judgment". (مَنْ كانَ يَرْجُوا لِقاءَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ لَآتٍ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ): (من) is a conditional noun that makes jussive, a mubtadaʾ; (كان) is a past incomplete verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the noun of (كان) is latent, referring to (من); the clause (يرجو) is the khabar of (كان); (لقاء الله) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إن أجل الله) is inna and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (آت) is the khabar of (إن); the wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ; and (السميع العليم) are two khabars of (من) [Translator's note: so in the text; evidently «of (هو)» is meant]. Further discussion of this verse will come in the section on rhetoric. The protasis and its apodosis are in the position of nominative as the khabar of (من).
(وَمَنْ جاهَدَ فَإِنَّما يُجاهِدُ لِنَفْسِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ عَنِ الْعالَمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (من) is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; (جاهد) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; the fāʾ links the answer; (إنما) is a restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (يجاهد) is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; (لنفسه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يجاهد); (إن) and its noun; the shifted lām; (غني) is the khabar of (إن); (عن العالمين) are attached to (غني); and the clause gives the reason for the preceding statement that no benefit reaches Allah from a person's striving. (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ لَنُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to (آمنوا); the lām prepares for the oath; (نكفرن) is an imperfect verb indeclinable on fatḥa, and the agent is latent, its implied form being "We"; the clause is the khabar of (الذين); (عنهم) are attached to (نكفرن); and (سيئاتهم) is the direct object. (وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَحْسَنَ الَّذِي كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ):
(لنجزينهم) is conjoined to (لنكفرن); (أحسن) is a second direct object; (الذي) is the muḍāf ilayhi; the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila; and the clause (يعملون) is the khabar of (كانوا).

* Rhetoric:
1- Expression by the verbal form and by the nominal form:
In His saying, Exalted is He, «فليعلمن الله الذين صدقوا وليعلمن الكاذبين» there is a difference between the verbal form, namely «صدقوا», and the nominal form in His saying «الكاذبين». The subtle point in this difference is that the active participle indicates the permanence of the maṣdar (verbal noun) in the agent and its being rooted in him, while the past verb does not indicate it; for at the time the verse was revealed it was a report about people newly come to Islam and about people persisting in unbelief, so He expressed the case of the former with the wording of the verb and the case of the latter with the form indicating permanence. As for Allah's knowledge, it is not to be said that there is in it a renewal in Allah the Exalted's knowledge of them before the testing, nor an implication that knowledge of what exists is other than knowledge that it will exist. The truth is that the knowledge of Allah the Exalted is one, attaching to the existent [Translator's note: the text has «بما لموجود», evidently for «بالموجود»] at the time of its existence, before it and after it, as it is. The benefit of mentioning knowledge here, even though it precedes the existence of what is known, is to point by the cause to the effect, which is recompense; as though He said: We shall surely know them and shall recompense them according to His knowledge of them.
2- Omission (al-ḥadhf):
In parsing His saying, Exalted is He, «من كان يرجو لقاء الله فإن أجل الله لآت» we proceeded on the basis that the fāʾ links the apodosis and that the clause (إن أجل الله لآت) is the answer. Its occurring as the answer to the condition is permissible — even though Allah's term is coming without doubt, unrestricted by any condition, [and an answer is one that] ceases to exist when the condition ceases — because by meeting Allah we mean that represented state, and the time in which that state occurs is the term appointed for death. It is as though He said: "Whoever hopes to meet Allah, the meeting with Allah is coming, because the term is that in which the meeting occurs", just as you say "whoever hopes to meet me, Friday is near", when it is known and customary that you sit to receive visitors on Friday. It may also be a case of rhetorical omission, the implied form being "so let him do righteous work and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord".

* Benefits:
The grammarians have gone at length in seeking the possible parsings of this verse, namely «أحسب الناس أن يتركوا أن يقولوا آمنا وهم لا يؤمنون» [Translator's note: so in the text; the Quranic wording is «وهم لا يفتنون»]. We have chosen the best of these parsings and the closest to logic, and we have also given the text of al-Zamakhsharī's saying about it; both views are acceptable and intended. We wish to detail for you the discussion of ẓann and ḥusbān and other verbs called "verbs of the heart" (afʿāl al-qulūb). They are so called because their meanings subsist in the heart. This does not mean that every verb of the heart puts two objects in the accusative; rather the verbs of the heart are of three kinds: one that does not pass to an object by itself, such as fakkara fī al-amr and tafakkara fīhi (he thought about the matter); one that passes to one object by itself, such as ʿarafa al-ḥaqq (he knew the truth) and fahima al-masʾala (he understood the question); and one that passes to two objects by itself, which is what is intended by the name. The origin of the two objects is mubtadaʾ and khabar. Some, namely al-Suhaylī, rejected this view and said: How can something like "I supposed Zayd to be ʿAmr" have as its origin a mubtadaʾ and khabar? It was answered that what is meant is likening, as shown by the fact that one says: "I supposed Zayd to be ʿAmr, then the contrary became clear", so the said supposing was due to his likening him to him. Some gave another answer, namely that it is interpreted as meaning "I supposed the thing named Zayd to be named ʿAmr", just as your saying "Zayd is Ḥātim" is interpreted as meaning "Zayd is like Ḥātim" in meaning. Listen to the saying of Zufar ibn al-Ḥārith al-Kilābī:
وكنا حسبنا كل بيضاء شحمة ... عشية لاقينا جذام وحميرا
(We had reckoned every white thing to be fat, on the evening we met Judhām and Ḥimyar.)
(كل بيضاء) is the first object of (حسبنا) and (شحمة) its second object; it is a metonymy (kināya) for his having supposed them cowards [Translator's note: the text has «شجعانا» (brave), which does not fit the sense of the line or the following «فتبينوا بخلاف ذلك»; translated according to the evident sense], and they proved otherwise. After this line:
فلما لقينا عصبة تغلبية ... يقودون جردا في الأعنّة خمرا
(When we met a Taghlibī band leading short-haired horses, lean, in their reins,)
سقيناهم كأسا سقونا بمثلها ... ولكنهم كانوا على الموت أصبرا
(we gave them to drink a cup the like of which they gave us to drink, but they were more steadfast in the face of death.)
فلما قرعنا النبع بالنبع بعضه ... ببعض أبت عيدانه أن تكسّرا
(When we struck nabʿ-wood against nabʿ-wood, one part against another, its sticks refused to break.)
When you know all this, you understand the meaning of the verse clearly, i.e.: Did those who made the word of testimony run on their tongues, boasted of it and lorded it over others, reckon that they would be left untested? No; rather Allah will test them with kinds of trial and types of ordeal until He sounds all their depths and tries their patience, the firmness of their feet and their being rooted in faith. For faith is not merely words repeated on tongues; rather it needs genuine work and continuous striving, so that their work may yield what benefits their community, and their striving may yield the firm establishment of their homelands.

dervis-irab:50-55.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقالُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آياتٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ): resumptive speech, to establish another kind of their obstinacy and arrogance. (قالوا) is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), referring to the unbelievers of Mecca; (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), equivalent to hallā; (أنزل) is a passive past verb; (عليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزل); (آيات) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (من ربه) is an adjective of (آيات), or is attached to (أنزل).
(قُلْ إِنَّمَا الْآياتُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَإِنَّما أَنَا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ): (إنما) is a restraining particle (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa) one; (الآيات) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (عند الله) is an adverb attached to an omitted element which is the khabar (predicate), i.e. He sends them down as He wills, with absolutely no involvement of anyone in that. (وإنما): the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial, and (إنما) is kāffa and makfūfa; (أنا) is a mubtadaʾ, (نذير) the khabar and (مبين) an adjective.
(أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ أَنَّا أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ يُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and affirmation (inkārī taqrīrī), and the wāw conjoins to an omitted, implied clause required by the context, i.e. "Did Muhammad fall short, and has it not sufficed them?" (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; (يكفهم) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم), and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (أن) and what follows it are the fāʿil of (يكفهم); anna and its noun, and the clause (أنزلنا عليك الكتاب) is the predicate of anna; the clause (يتلى عليهم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَرَحْمَةً وَذِكْرى لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ): (إن) is a particle resembling the verb; (في ذلك) is its fronted predicate; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (رحمة) is its postponed noun; (ذكرى) is conjoined to (رحمة); (لقوم) is an adjective of (ذكرى); and the clause (يؤمنون) is an adjective of (قوم).
(قُلْ كَفى بِاللَّهِ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ شَهِيداً يَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): (كفى) is a past verb; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and the Name of Majesty is genitive by the bāʾ in form, being the fāʿil of (كفى), nominative in position; (بيني) is an adverb attached to (شهيدا); (بينكم) is conjoined to (شهيدا) [Translator's note: so in the source; it is conjoined to «بيني»]; (شهيدا) is a tamyīz (specification); the clause (يعلم) is a ḥāl; (ما) is the object of (يعلم); (في السموات) is the ṣila (relative clause); and (الأرض) is conjoined to (السموات).
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِالْباطِلِ وَكَفَرُوا بِاللَّهِ أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ): (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; (بالباطل) is attached to (آمنوا); (وكفروا بالله) is conjoined to (آمنوا بالباطل); (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); (الخاسرون) is the predicate of (هم) or the predicate of (أولئك); and the clause is the predicate of (الذين).
(وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالْعَذابِ وَلَوْلا أَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى لَجاءَهُمُ الْعَذابُ): resumptive speech, introduced to express wonder at them or mockery of them. (يستعجلونك) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the kāf a mafʿūl bihi; (بالعذاب) is attached to (يستعجلونك); (لولا) is a particle of non-occurrence due to the existence [of something]; (أجل) is a mubtadaʾ and (مسمى) its adjective, the predicate being omitted; the lām links the answer; (جاءهم العذاب) is a verb, a mafʿūl bihi and a fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(وَلَيَأْتِيَنَّهُمْ بَغْتَةً وَهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); (يأتينهم) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi; (بغتة) is a ḥāl; the wāw is circumstantial; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا يشعرون) is the khabar; the clause (هم لا يشعرون) is a ḥāl.
(يَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالْعَذابِ وَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ لَمُحِيطَةٌ بِالْكافِرِينَ): the i'rab of (يستعجلونك بالعذاب) has preceded. The clause was repeated to express wonder at their foolishness, because whoever is threatened with something seeks the means of protection from it, whereas these hasten it on. The wāw is circumstantial; inna and its noun; the shifted lām; (محيطة) is the predicate of inna; (بالكافرين) is attached to (محيطة). He expressed it with the present and meant the future, i.e. it will encompass them, to indicate certainty and for hyperbole. It is also possible that by Jahannam its causes leading to it are meant, in which case there is no figurative interpretation in His saying (محيطة).
(يَوْمَ يَغْشاهُمُ الْعَذابُ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ): the adverb is attached to (محيطة); the clause (يغشاهم العذاب) is in the position of the genitive, the adverb being annexed to it; (من فوقهم) is a ḥāl, and (من تحت أرجلهم) is conjoined to (من فوقهم).
(وَيَقُولُ ذُوقُوا ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (يقول) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", referring to the one in charge of the punishment; it was also read (ونقول). In either case the clause is conjoined to (يغشاهم). The clause (ذوقوا) is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying), being an imperative verb and its fāʿil; (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi on the assumption of a muḍāf, i.e. "the recompense of what"; the clause (كنتم) is the ṣila, and the clause (تعملون) is the predicate of (كنتم).

* Rhetoric:
Allah, Glorified and Exalted, specified the fire of Jahannam with the upper and lower sides and did not mention the right, the left, behind or in front, to show the difference between it and the fire of this world, which surrounds from all sides. The fire of Jahannam is not extinguished by treading on it, but it comes down from above.

dervis-irab:56-59.t:
* I'rab:
(يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّ أَرْضِي واسِعَةٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَاعْبُدُونِ): (يا) is a vocative particle; (عبادي) is the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the yāʾ of the first person; (الذين) is an adjective of (عبادي); the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila (relative clause); inna, its noun and its predicate. The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ of eloquence), i.e. if a place becomes narrow for you, then worship Me alone. (إياي) is the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "worship Me alone (uʿbudū iyyāya)", one of the two verbs sufficing for the other. (فاعبدون): the fāʾ conjoins to the first fāʾ, and the clause (اعبدوني) is explicative (tafsīriyya); it is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), which is the omitted yāʾ.
(كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ ثُمَّ إِلَيْنا تُرْجَعُونَ): (كل نفس) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (ذائقة الموت) is its khabar (predicate), what is meant being its bitterness and hardship; (ثم) is a conjunction for sequence with delay; (إلينا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ترجعون); (ترجعون) is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ غُرَفاً تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها نِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعامِلِينَ): (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; the clause (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to the clause (آمنوا); the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); (نبوئنهم) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "naḥnu", and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi; the oath clause is the predicate of (الذين). You may also put (الذين) in the accusative by an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned after it, namely (نبوئنهم). (من الجنة) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (غرفا) is a second object, because bawwaʾa is transitive to two objects, and its like has passed in Yūnus and al-Ḥajj; the clause (تجري من تحتها الأنهار) is an adjective of (غرفا); (خالدين فيها) is a ḥāl; (نعم) is an invariable (jāmid) past verb for expressing praise; (أجر العاملين) is the fāʿil of (نعم), and the one specified for praise is omitted, i.e. "their reward".
(الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَلى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ): (الذين) is an adjective (naʿt) of (العاملين). You may also cut it off, putting it in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, or in the accusative as accusative of praise by an omitted verb, its implied form being "I praise". The clause (صبروا) is the ṣila; (على ربهم) is attached to (يتوكلون); (يتوكلون) is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. Patience here is general, including emigration, leaving the homeland, the harm of the polytheists and other things to which the Muslims were exposed at the outset of their affair; and its rulings apply to everyone whom the calamities of the days and the misfortunes of time have tested.

dervis-irab:60-64.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَقْدِرُ): He straitens and restricts. This verb has remarkable characteristics, for it is distributed over a number of meanings, which we will deal with below:
One says: qadara the provision: He apportioned it, of the patterns of naṣara and ḍaraba; and qadara and qaddara on his dependants: he straitened and restricted. He said in al-Asās: "His provision was qadara and qaddara upon him: restricted." Qadira yaqdaru, of the pattern of ʿalima, [with the maṣdars] qudran, qudratan, maqdaratan, maqdiratan, maqduratan, miqdāran, qadāratan, qudūratan, qudūran, qidrānan, qadāran and qadaran ʿalā al-shayʾ: he was powerful over it. Qadara yaqdiru, of the pattern of ḍaraba, qadran the matter: he planned it; qadara a thing by a thing: he measured it against it [Translator's note: the source has «فاسه», a misprint for «قاسه»] and made it according to its measure. Qadara yaqduru and yaqdiru, of the two patterns of naṣara and jalasa, Allah: he magnified Him. Qadara the man: he thought about arranging and managing his affair. Qadira yaqdaru, of the pattern of taʿiba, qadaran with two fatḥas: his neck was short. Qadara ʿalā al-shayʾ: he was able to do it (iqtadara).
(الْحَيَوانُ): the maṣdar (verbal noun) of ḥayiya; its regular form is ḥayayān, and the second yāʾ was changed to wāw, as Sībawayh said. Whatever has life in it was called ḥayawān. They said: "Buy the mawatān and do not buy the ḥayawān", i.e. buy land and houses and do not buy slaves and beasts. In the form ḥayawān there is an additional meaning not present in the form ḥayāt, namely what the faʿalān pattern carries of the meaning of movement and agitation, as in nazawān (leaping), lahabān (blazing) and the like. Life is movement, just as death is stillness; so its coming in a form indicating the meaning of movement is a hyperbole in the meaning of life, and for this reason it was chosen over ḥayāt in this context, which calls for hyperbole.

* I'rab:
(وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا): resumptive speech, introduced to establish reliance on Allah and the absence of anxiety. The i'rab of (كأين) has preceded in detail; here it is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (من دابة) is its tamyīz (specification), made genitive by (من); the clause (لا تحمل رزقها) is an adjective of (دابة). His saying (اللَّهُ يَرْزُقُها وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ) is the khabar (predicate): (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يرزقها) is the predicate of (الله); (إياكم) is conjoined to the hāʾ; the wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, (السميع) a first predicate and (العليم) a second predicate.
(وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); (إن) is conditional; (سألتهم) is a past verb, the tāʾ being the fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (من) is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the clause (خلق السموات والأرض) is the predicate of (من), and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the second object of (سألتهم), which is suspended by the interrogative; (وسخر الشمس والقمر) is conjoined to (خلق السموات والأرض). The lām occurs in the answer to the oath; (يقولن) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of identical letters; the wāw of the plural, dropped because two quiescent letters met, is the fāʿil, and the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis. (الله) is the predicate of an omitted subject, its implied form being "huwa", or a mubtadaʾ whose predicate is omitted, its implied form being "Allah created the heavens". The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ of eloquence); (أنى) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); (يؤفكون) is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
(اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ مِنْ عِبادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ): (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يبسط الرزق) the khabar; (لمن) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يبسط); the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila (relative clause); (من عباده) is a ḥāl; (يقدر) is an imperfect verb conjoined to (يبسط); (له) is attached to (يقدر), the pronoun referring to (من); inna and its noun; (عليم) is its predicate, and (بكل شيء) is attached to (عليم).
(وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ نَزَّلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَأَحْيا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْتِها لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ): conjoined to the preceding clause, and it is identical to it in its i'rab.
(قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لا يَعْقِلُونَ): (الحمد) is a mubtadaʾ and (لله) the khabar, the clause being the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying); (بل) is a particle of turning away (iḍrāb); (أكثرهم) is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (لا يعقلون) is the khabar.
(وَما هذِهِ الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (ما) is negative; (هذه) is a mubtadaʾ; (الحياة) is a badal (substitute); (الدنيا) is an adjective (naʿt) of (الحياة); (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (لهو) is the predicate of (هذه); and (لعب) is conjoined to (لهو).
(وَإِنَّ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ الْحَيَوانُ لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; inna and its noun; (الآخرة) is an adjective of (الدار); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (هي) is a mubtadaʾ and (الحيوان) the khabar, the clause being the predicate of inna; (لو) is conditional; kāna and its noun, and the clause (يعلمون) is its predicate. The apodosis (jawāb) of (لو) is omitted, i.e. "they would not have preferred the life of this world".

dervis-irab:8-11.t:
* I'rab:
(وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ حُسْناً): resumptive speech, beginning the establishment of the right of the parents and limiting obedience to them by not disobeying Allah. (وصينا) is a verb and its agent; (الإنسان) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بوالديه) are attached (mutaʿalliq) to (وصينا); and (حسنا) is a naʿt (adjective) of the maṣdar (verbal noun) of (وصينا), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "an enjoining possessing goodness", or it is in itself goodness, by way of hyperbole. Al-Zajjāj said: "Its meaning is: We enjoined on man that he should do with his parents what is good" [Translator's note: the text has «وما يحسن», with an apparently stray wāw]. (وَإِنْ جاهَداكَ لِتُشْرِكَ بِي ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ فَلا تُطِعْهُما): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (جاهداك) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the alif is the fāʿil (agent) and the kāf the direct object. In (لتشرك) the lām is the lām of causation and (تشرك) is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of causation; the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (جاهداك). (بي) are attached to (تشرك); (ما) is a relative noun, the direct object of (تشرك); (لك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) put first; (به) are attached to (علم); (علم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) put after; and the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما). In (فلا) the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because the answer is a clause [unfit to be a protasis]; (لا) is prohibitive; (تطعهما) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لا), and the agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; the mīm and alif are two letters indicating the dual; and the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of jussive as the answer of (إن). (إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ): (إلي) is a khabar put first and (مرجعكم) a mubtadaʾ put after; the fāʾ is a conjunction; (أنبئكم) is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "I", and the kāf is the direct object; (بما) are attached to (أنبئكم); the clause (كنتم) is the ṣila of (ما); and the clause (تعملون) is the khabar of (كنتم).
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ لَنُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ فِي الصَّالِحِينَ): (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «لندخلنهم في الصالحين», i.e. in the company of those firmly rooted in righteousness. It may also be in the position of accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb). The clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; the clause (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to the clause (آمنوا); the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (ندخلن) is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, whose agent is latent, its implied form being "We"; the hāʾ is the direct object; and (في الصالحين) are attached to (ندخلهم) [Translator's note: so in the text, for «ندخلنهم»].
(وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ): resumptive speech, set out to describe the condition of the hypocrites after He had described the condition of the believers and the unbelievers in what precedes. (من الناس) is a khabar put first; (من) is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), a mubtadaʾ put after, i.e. "people"; this is better than making it a relative. The clause (يقول) is an adjective of (من) according to its wording; the clause (آمنا) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); and (بالله) are attached to (آمنا). (فَإِذا أُوذِيَ فِي اللَّهِ جَعَلَ فِتْنَةَ النَّاسِ كَعَذابِ اللَّهِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (إذا) is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; (في الله) are attached to (أوذي); the clause (أوذي) is in the position of genitive through the adverb being put in construct (iḍāfa) with it — i.e. "in the way of Allah"; the clause (جعل) has no position because it is the answer of (إذا); (فتنة الناس) is the first object of (جعل); and (كعذاب الله) is in the position of the second object, or the kāf is a noun meaning "like", in the position of the second object. The meaning is: he was alarmed at people's harm and so obeyed them as one who fears Allah obeys Allah. (وَلَئِنْ جاءَ نَصْرٌ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ إِنَّا كُنَّا مَعَكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām prepares for the oath; (إن) is a conditional particle that makes jussive; (جاءهم) [Translator's note: so in the text; the Quranic wording is «جاء»] is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis, and the hāʾ is the direct object; (نصر) is the agent; (من ربك) are attached to (جاءهم) or to an omitted adjective of (نصر). In (ليقولن) the lām occurs in the answer of the oath, and (يقولن) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the presence of the nūn, which was dropped because of a succession of like letters; the wāw of the plural, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the agent. The clause (إنا) is the object of the saying; (إن) and its noun, and the clause (كنا) is its khabar; and (معكم) is an adverb attached to the omitted khabar of (كنا). (أَوَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِأَعْلَمَ بِما فِي صُدُورِ الْعالَمِينَ): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation and rebuke, and the wāw is conjoined to something omitted that the context calls for; (ليس) is a past incomplete verb and (الله) its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (أعلم) is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of (ليس); (بما) are attached to (أعلم); and (في صدور العالمين) is the ṣila of (ما). (وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām prepares for the oath; (يعلمن) is an imperfect verb indeclinable on fatḥa; (الله) is the agent; (الذين) is the direct object; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; and (وليعلمن المنافقين) is conjoined to (وليعلمن الذين آمنوا).

* Benefits:
History relates that when Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, one of the foremost to embrace Islam, became Muslim, his mother — she [Translator's note: the text repeats «وهي وهي»] being Ḥamna bint Abī Sufyān ibn Umayya ibn ʿAbd Shams — said: "Saʿd, I have heard that you have turned Ṣābiʾ. By Allah, no roof of a house shall shade me from the sun (al-ḍiḥḥ) and the wind, and food and drink are forbidden to me, until you disbelieve in Muḥammad." He was the dearest of her children to her. Saʿd refused, and she remained like that for three days. So Saʿd came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and complained to him, and this verse was revealed, together with the one in Luqmān and the one in al-Aḥqāf. The Messenger of Allah ordered him to treat her gently and seek to please her with kindness.
In a narration of al-Qurṭubī, Saʿd said to her: "By Allah, if you had a hundred souls and they went out one soul after another, I would not disbelieve in Muḥammad; so if you wish, eat, and if you wish, do not eat." When she saw that, she ate. As for the meaning of her saying "By Allah, no roof of a house shall shade me from the ḍiḥḥ and the wind", as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, al-ḍiḥḥ is the sun; and in the ḥadīth: "Let none of you sit between the sun (al-ḍiḥḥ) and the shade, for it is the sitting-place of Satan." It has also been said that it was revealed concerning ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿa al-Makhzūmī [Translator's note: the text has «عياش بن ربيعة»]. That is, he emigrated with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, the two travelling together, until they reached Medina. Then Abū Jahl ibn Hishām and al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, his brothers through his mother Asmāʾ bint Makhrama, a woman of Banū Tamīm ibn Ḥanẓala, set out, came to ʿAyyāsh and said to him: "Part of Muḥammad's religion is maintaining the ties of kinship and dutifulness to parents, and you have left your mother not eating, not drinking and not taking shelter in a house until she sees you, and she loves you more than we do; so come out with us." And they "twisted at his hump and withers" (i.e. kept working on him). He consulted ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The two are deceiving you, and I undertake to divide my wealth between me and you." But they kept at him until he obeyed them and disobeyed ʿUmar. ʿUmar said to him: "Since you have disobeyed me, take my she-camel, for there is no camel in the world that can catch her; if anything about them makes you suspicious, go back." When they reached al-Baydāʾ, Abū Jahl said: "My she-camel is exhausted, so carry me with you." He said: "Yes," and dismounted to make a place for himself and for him. They seized him, tied him firmly, each of them flogged him a hundred lashes, and they took him to his mother, who said: "You will remain in torment until you turn back from the religion of Muḥammad." So it was revealed.
Whether the occasion was this or that, the matter is general: dutifulness to parents is required by the Law and obeying them is obligatory, except in disobedience, for there is no obedience to a creature in disobedience to the Creator. As for the saying «وفتلا منه في الذروة والغارب», al-Jawharī said in his Ṣiḥāḥ: "So-and-so kept twisting at so-and-so's hump and withers, i.e. he went round behind him to deceive him."

dervis-irab:65-69.t:
* I'rab:
(فَإِذا رَكِبُوا فِي الْفُلْكِ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ of eloquence), because it discloses something omitted, indicated by the description and explanation of their affair, namely that they are as described, in polytheism and obstinacy. It is not unlikely that it is resumptive, in order to move on to another pattern of their obstinacy. (إذا) is an adverb of the future containing the meaning of a condition; the clause (ركبوا) is in the position of the genitive, the adverb being annexed to it; (في الفلك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ركبوا); the clause (دعوا الله) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; (مخلصين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (له) is attached to (مخلصين); and (الدين) is the object of (مخلصين), because it is an active participle.
(فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ إِذا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (لما) is temporal, meaning "when" (ḥīniyya), or a linking particle; (نجاهم) is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إلى البر) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (نجاهم); (إذا) is the particle of surprise (fujāʾiyya), and together with what it enters upon it forms a clause with no grammatical position, because it is the answer of (لما); (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (يشركون) is the predicate of (هم).
(لِيَكْفُرُوا بِما آتَيْناهُمْ وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ): the lām is the lām of kay (purpose), and (يتمتعوا) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb directly after this lām is «يكفروا»] is an imperfect verb, accusative by (أن) implied after the lām of kay; (بما) is attached to (يكفروا); the clause (آتيناهم) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما); (وليتمتعوا) is conjoined to (ليكفروا) and so is like it. The lām in both may also be the lām of consequence and outcome (lām al-ʿāqiba wal-maʾāl), and it is possible that the lām in both is the lām of command; (وليتمتعوا) was also read with a quiescent lām, as a command of threat. A full discussion of the meaning of the command will come in the section on rhetoric, as will al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad's discussion of the types of lām in the Arabic language in the section on benefits. The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa; (سوف) is a particle of the future; and (يعلمون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil.
(أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنا حَرَماً آمِناً وَيُتَخَطَّفُ النَّاسُ مِنْ حَوْلِهِمْ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī) conveying affirmation (taqrīr), because when the hamza of disapproving interrogation enters a negation it conveys affirmation, since the speech becomes positive. The wāw conjoins to an omitted clause, its implied form being "We have made them secure, settled in Mecca, and did they not know that?". (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; (يروا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم), and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أن) and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of (يروا); anna and its noun, and the clause (جعلنا) is its predicate. The first object of (جعلنا) is omitted, i.e. "We made their town, Mecca"; (حرما) is a second mafʿūl bihi and (آمنا) an adjective; the wāw is circumstantial; (يتخطف) is a passive imperfect verb; (الناس) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (من حولهم) is a ḥāl.
(أَفَبِالْباطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ وَبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَكْفُرُونَ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval, and the fāʾ conjoins to an omitted clause; (بالباطل) is attached to (يؤمنون); and (وبنعمة الله يكفرون) is conjoined to what precedes it.
(وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِالْحَقِّ لَمَّا جاءَهُ): the wāw is resumptive; (من) is an interrogative noun containing the meaning of negation, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; (أظلم) is the khabar (predicate); (ممن) is attached to (أظلم); the clause (افترى على الله) is the ṣila; (كذبا) is a mafʿūl bihi; (أو) is a conjunction; (كذب) is conjoined to (افترى); (بالحق) is attached to (كذب); (لما) is temporal or a linking particle; and (جاءه) is a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi.
(أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوىً لِلْكافِرِينَ): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīrī); (ليس) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; (في جهنم) is the fronted predicate of laysa; (مثوى) is its postponed noun; and (للكافرين) is an adjective of (مثوى). The meaning of affirmation will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَالَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا فِينا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنا وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (جاهدوا) is the ṣila, and the object of (جاهدوا) is omitted; the secret of its omission will come in the section on rhetoric. (فينا) is attached to (جاهدوا): in Our cause and for Our sake, and purely for Our face. The lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); the clause (نهدينهم) is the predicate of (الذين); (سبلنا) is a second mafʿūl bihi, or accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ); inna and its noun; and (مع المحسنين) is an adverb attached to an omitted predicate of inna.

* Rhetoric:
1- The meaning of the command:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how is it permissible for Allah to command unbelief, and that the disobedient do whatever they wish, when He forbids that and threatens punishment for it? I say: it is a figurative expression for abandonment and leaving [them] to themselves, and that this command is extremely displeasing. Its example is that you see a man who has resolved on a matter, and you hold that this matter is a mistake and will lead to great harm; so you go to great lengths in advising him and bringing him down from his opinion. When you see nothing from him but refusal and determination, you become angry with him (ḥaridta, i.e. you became angry) and say: You and your affair; do what you wish. You do not intend by this a real command — how could you, when the one who commands a thing wants it, while you strongly dislike it and are grieved? Rather, it is as if you were saying to him: since you have refused to accept advice, you deserve to be told 'do what you wish', so that it becomes clear to you, when you do it, that the adviser's opinion was sound and yours was corrupt."
2- The interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī):
We said that when the hamza of disapproval enters a negation, it becomes positive and returns to the meaning of affirmation. Of this in poetry is the saying of Jarīr praising ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān:
ألستم خير من ركب المطايا ... وأندى العالمين بطون راح
(Are you not the best of those who ever rode mounts, and the most generous of all the worlds in the palms of their hands?)
Some said: had it been a question, the caliph would not have given him a hundred camels. It is said that when Jarīr reached this verse in the ode, ʿAbd al-Malik was reclining, and he sat up straight in delight and said: "This is how we are to be praised", and gave him a hundred camels.
3- Omission (ḥadhf):
The discussion of omitting the mafʿūl bihi for concision has preceded, and here it is in His saying «والذين جاهدوا فينا». He left the striving unrestricted and did not restrict it with an object, so that it includes everything that must be striven against: the soul that incites to evil, and Satan. This is better than assuming a specific object, as many of the commentators did, so that it includes all acts of obedience and means of drawing near [Translator's note: the source has «المزدلفات»; probably «المُزْلِفات» (means of drawing near) is meant].

* Benefits:
The mention of the lāms by al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad al-Farāhīdī:
Al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad, the teacher of Sībawayh, mentioned in a small treatise of his that the number of lāms is forty-one. We present them with a brief indication of their rulings, as al-Khalīl presented them, and then comment on some [Translator's note: the source has «على ما بعض», apparently a transposition of «على بعض ما»] of them which we consider worthy of comment:
1- The lām of the oath: it has the fatḥa and is followed by a doubled nūn, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: «لترون الجحيم ثم لترونها عين اليقين ثم لتسألنّ يومئذ عن النعيم».
2- The lām of the answer to the oath: it resembles the lām of the oath and takes its place.
3- The lām of command: it never comes except after a wāw or a fāʾ, as in His saying, the Exalted, «فليعبدوا ربّ هذا البيت», «ولتأت طائفة» and the like. If there is no wāw or fāʾ, the lām has the kasra, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: «لينفق ذو سعة من سعته».
4- The lām of the answer to a command: it resembles the lām of command, and I know only one instance of it, namely His saying, Mighty and Majestic: «ولنحمل خطاياكم», and no other.
5- The lām of promise: it resembles the lām of command and takes its place; I know only two instances in the Quran, namely in His saying, the Exalted: «فليستجيبوا لي وليؤمنوا بي».
6- The lām of threat: it resembles the lām of command and takes its place; I know only four instances in the Quran, namely in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: «فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفّر», and like it «فليضحكوا قليلا وليبكوا كثيرا», and no others.
7- The lām of emphasis (tawkīd): it has the fatḥa and is preceded by a doubled nūn; it comes only after inna, innā, a-innaka, innakum, innahum, innahumā and innahu, as in His saying, the Exalted: «وإن الله لعليم حليم», «إن الله لغفور رحيم», «إننا لفي شك», «يقول أإنك لمن المصدقين», «وإنكم لتمرون عليهم مصبحين», «وإنه لحب الخير لشديد», «إن هؤلاء لشرذمة قليلون».
8- The lām of support (ʿimād): it has the fatḥa and comes only after kāda, I mean: «وإن يكاد الذين كفروا ليزلقونك بأبصارهم», «وإن كادوا ليستفزونك» and the like.
9- The lām of denial (juḥd): it has the kasra in itself and puts the verb in the accusative; it comes only after kāna, mā kunnā and mā kānū — by this I mean [forms of] being — as in His saying: «وما كان الله ليطلعكم على الغيب», «وما كانوا ليؤمنوا» and the like.
10- The lām of kay: it has the kasra in itself and puts the verb in the accusative; it never comes except after a verb that has passed, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: «ولتجري الفلك» and the like.
11- The lām of the light in [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably the lām associated with the light an is meant]: it has the kasra and resembles the lām of kay, taking its place, as in His saying, the Exalted: «وأمرنا لنسلم لرب العالمين», «يريدون ليطفئوا نور الله بأفواهم», «ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى».
12- The lām of outcome (ghāya): it resembles the lām of kay and takes its place, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: «ليضلوا عن سبيلك».
13- The lām of hope (tarajjī): it has the fatḥa, as in His saying, the Exalted: «لعل الله يحدث بعد ذلك أمرا», «لعلك باخع نفسك», «لعله يذكّر أو يخشى».
14- The lām of wish (tamannī): it has the fatḥa, as in His saying, the Exalted: «يا ليتني كنت ترابا», «يا ليتنا نرد ولا نكذب بآيات ربنا».
15- The lām of warning (taḥdhīr): I know only one instance in the Quran, namely His saying, Mighty and Majestic: «لا يحطمنكم سليمان وجنوده وهم لا يشعرون», and no other.
16- The lām of praise: it has the fatḥa; of this is «لنعم دار المتقين».
17- The lām of blame: it also has the fatḥa; of this is «لبئس المولى ولبئس العشير».
18- The lām of "kamā" (just as): it has the fatḥa; I know only one instance in the Quran, namely His saying: «وإذا أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين لما آتيتكم من كتاب وحكمة», the meaning being "just as I gave you".
19- The transposed lām (al-manqūl): it has the fatḥa, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: «يدعو لمن ضره أقرب من نفعه», «ولمن صبر وغفر», the meaning being "the one who harms him" and "the one who is patient".
20- The lām of requital (jazāʾ): it always has the fatḥa and comes only after law and lawlā, as in His saying, the Exalted: «ولو شئنا لبعثنا», «ولو شئنا لرفعناه بها» and the like.
21- The lām of affirmation (ījāb): it has the fatḥa and never comes except after the light in, as in His saying, the Exalted: «وإن كل ذلك لما متاع الحياة الدنيا», «وإن كلّ لما جميع لدينا محضرون» and the like.
22- The lām of intercession (shafāʿa): it has the kasra in itself; I know only one instance in the Quran, namely His saying, Mighty and Majestic: «ليقض علينا ربك».
23- The lām of calling for help (istighātha): it is the redundant lām of the genitive, as in: yā la-Zaydin.
24- The lām of the genitive (jarr): it has the kasra in itself and puts what follows in the genitive, as in lil-muʾminīn, lil-ʿālamīn and the like.
25- The lām of the attribute (ṣifa): it has the fatḥa in itself and puts what follows in the genitive; examples: wa-lanā, wa-lakum, laka, lahu and the like. This lām was given the fatḥa and the lām of the genitive the kasra only to distinguish between the pronoun and the overt noun.
26- The radical lām (aṣl): it is quiescent, as in al-ḥasana, al-sayyiʾa, al-wālidāt and the like.
27- The lām of definiteness (maʿrifa): it is quiescent and augmentative, and serves for making definite, as in al-rajul, al-ghulām, al-jāriya, al-muʾminīn, al-muttaqīn and the like.
28- The lām of plurality (taktīr): it has the fatḥa and is a radical lām, as in ulāʾika, ulāʾikum, ulātu ḥaml and the like. It was called the lām of plurality only because you address the singular with a plural word.
29- The lām of inception (ibtidāʾ): it has the fatḥa, as in «ولذكر الله أكبر», «لقالوا إنما سكرت أبصارنا», «لعمرك إنهم لفي سكرتهم يعمهون».
30- The lām of preference (tafḍīl): it resembles the lām of inception and takes its place, as in His saying, the Exalted: «ولعبد مؤمن خير من مشرك», and like it «لمسجد أسس على التقوى» and the like.
31- The lām of laysa: it has the fatḥa, as in His saying, the Exalted: «لا يعلمون», «لا يسمعون», «لا يألونكم خبالا» and the like.
32- The lām of negation (nafy): it has the fatḥa and resembles the lām of laysa, taking its place, as in His saying, the Exalted: «ولا أقول لكم عندي خزائن الله ولا أعلم الغيب», «ولا أقول للذين تزدري أعينكم», the meaning being "nor do I say to you".
33- The lām of "ghayr" (other than): it has the fatḥa and conjoins what follows it to what precedes it, as in His saying, the Exalted: «لا فارض ولا بكر عوان بين ذلك», «لا شرقية ولا غربية», «لا ظليل ولا يغني من اللهب» and the like.
34- The lām of exoneration (tabriʾa): it has the fatḥa and puts indefinite nouns in the accusative, as in His saying, the Exalted: «لا ريب فيه», «لا إكراه», «لا تثريب», «لا جرم» and the like.
35- The lām of connection (ṣila): it has the fatḥa and comes only after denial, as in His saying, the Exalted: «لا الشمس ينبغي لها أن تدرك القمر ولا الليل سابق النهار» and the like.
36- The lām of prohibition (nahy): it has the fatḥa in itself and puts what follows in the jussive, as in His saying: «فلا يسرف في القتل»; 37- «ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم», «ولا تتبع الهوى» and the like. [Translator's note: the numbering 36–37 runs together like this in the source.]
38- The lām of supplication (duʿāʾ): it resembles the lām of prohibition and takes its place, as in His saying, the Exalted: «ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به», «ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا».
39- The lām of entitlement (istiḥqāq): it has the ḍamma at the end of the word, as in wayl wherever it occurs. Al-Khalīl said: "The lām is complete, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds."
Remarks:
1- In the explanation he did not mention the lām of annexation (ilḥāq) and the lām of eloquence (faṣāḥa), although he had counted them at first.
2- He counted «لا» as a lām, which is contrary to the practice of the grammarians.
As for Ibn Hishām, he divided the single lām into three types: governing the genitive, governing the jussive, and non-governing; there is no type governing the accusative in the division, contrary to the Kufans. The one governing the genitive has the kasra with every overt noun, as in li-Zaydin and li-ʿAmrin, except with the one called for help directly after it, where it has the fatḥa, as in yā la-llāhi; and it has the fatḥa with every pronoun, as in lanā, lakum and lahum, except with the yāʾ of the first person, where it has the kasra.
The genitive lām has twenty-two meanings, which he mentioned in the book al-Mughnī; let whoever wishes refer to it.
Then he spoke about the lām governing the jussive. As for the non-governing lām, it is of seven kinds: the lām of inception; the redundant lām; the lām of the answer; the lām entering a conditional particle to announce that the answer after it is built on an oath before it, not on the condition, hence it is called the lām preparing for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); the lām of al; the lām attached to demonstratives to indicate distance; and the non-genitive lām of wonder. The details are in the book al-Mughnī.
